findings.reason: as written three of the ten assertions cannot hold, so a worker either writes controls that fail for reasons unrelated to its change or quietly drops them, and the node's falsifiability rests on the seven that remain.
findings.text: three of §7's ten negative controls name the wrong case numbers: "accepting a log with no EXIT= line accepts the eighth case" would leave the eighth case (a pytest gate with no summary) still refused, the no-EXIT= case being the seventh; "holding only non-pytest commands to a summary accepts the ninth" would accept the eighth case and refuse the ninth, since the ninth is the ctest log; and "requiring a pytest summary refuses the seventh case, the ctest log" names the ctest case the seventh when it is the ninth — the insertion of the two new refusal cases ahead of it shifted every reference that named the ctest case by two

findings.reason: the sixth case asserts only that the refusal names the fields, so without the monkeypatched case a literal list in the message passes every case listed and the anti-drift guarantee §8 states is unproven.
findings.text: §8's third negative control, "restating the field list as literals in the refusal fails a case that adds a field to the function under monkeypatch", names a case that is not among the six cases the done-when lists, so the control has nothing to fail and the "read from that function's fields, not restated" obligation is never exercised

findings.reason: a coordinator following the chain the plan itself carries would build every section except the newly declared one, so the section that reads `test_logs` and glued suite observations would be left undispatched with its two reproduced defects unfixed.
findings.text: the followup that sequences the build names §2, then §4 and §5, then §6 and §7, and never §8, although the same change declares s8 implementable with a wait on §7

findings.reason: the meta's operative claim is that no live plan waits on this one and it waits on none, which §8 does not change, so the enumeration is descriptive drift a reader corrects from the section table.
findings.text: `plan-standalone` enumerates five repairs (the red-base id match, commit coverage, the shared failure-matching rule, the post-landing worktree release and the receipt-versus-log figures) while the plan now carries §8 as a sixth (reading a manifest's gate evidence in the shapes workers write it)
